title: Thomas Becket (29 December)
hook: the archbishop killed in his own cathedral

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Evangelist, the disciple whom Jesus loved, his head resting on Jesus at supper. Your line was the beloved disciple.

Late afternoon, winter, Canterbury. The monks are singing the evening office when armed knights come in from the cloister, looking for the archbishop. His monks run to bolt the doors behind him. He stops them. Edward Grim, a visiting cleric, heard what the archbishop said: a church is not to be made into a castle. Leave the doors open. A few minutes later, Thomas Becket was dead on the floor of his own cathedral. How did the king's friend end up there?
screen: `EVENING PRAYER AT CANTERBURY.` → `KNIGHTS IN THE CLOISTER.` → `LEAVE THE DOORS OPEN.`

segments.voice: Thomas started as the king's man: chancellor to King Henry the Second, his friend and right hand, famous for fine clothes and a big household. When the archbishop of Canterbury died, Henry pushed to put Thomas in the job, expecting a friend at the head of the English Church. He got a different man. The old accounts say Thomas began to live simply under his robes and to pray long hours. And he started saying no to the king, above all over whether clergy accused of crimes would be tried in the king's courts or the Church's. The quarrel turned bitter. Thomas fled into exile in France and stayed away a long time. A fragile peace brought him home. Then Henry, angry at news from Canterbury, said something in his hall. Nobody agrees on the exact words; the line you may have heard about a troublesome priest is a later retelling. But some knights heard it as permission and rode for the cathedral. Grim, who tried to shield the archbishop and was wounded himself, says Thomas died commending himself and the Church to God. Why is this a feast and not just a murder story? Jesus says in John's Gospel, in the Douay-Rheims, "I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd giveth his life for his sheep." The accounts don't make Thomas gentle; he could be proud and stubborn. Yet at the end he stood still and kept the door open. Chroniclers say the king himself later came to the tomb in penance, and pilgrims kept coming to Canterbury long after.
screen: `THE KING'S FRIEND AND CHANCELLOR.` · `THE ARCHBISHOP WHO SAID NO.` · `KILLED IN HIS OWN CATHEDRAL.` · `THE GOOD SHEPHERD GIVETH HIS LIFE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who carries responsibility for a community, a bishop, a parish priest, a youth minister, the person who runs your local shelter, and picture them at the end of a long day, facing a hard decision. If you pray, ask that they have courage when they need to say no, and humility when they don't; if you don't pray, simply hold them in your attention and wish them a clear head.
Thomas Becket. The king's friend who became archbishop of Canterbury, stood against the king, and was killed in his own cathedral with the doors left open. Today's word.
Your line: killed in the cathedral. The doors stayed open. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics may keep Saint Thomas Becket's memorial on 29 December, inside the Christmas octave, and in England his feast is kept with special honor; pilgrims still visit the place of his martyrdom in Canterbury Cathedral.

chat.meaning: As archbishop he said no to Henry over the Church's courts and died in his cathedral; his feast recalls the good shepherd who gives his life.

notes: Outline hook's year (1170) and the number of knights deliberately left out under the claims rule; the index hook line here drops the year. Owner may restore if a cited source is added.

Grim's report that Becket refused to bar the doors ('a church is not to be made into a castle', paraphrased) and his last words commending himself and the Church to God: confirm paraphrase against Grim.
'The line about a troublesome priest is a later retelling': confirm framing (the 'turbulent priest' wording is not in contemporary sources).
The quarrel summarized as over criminous clerks (clergy accused of crimes) and royal vs church courts; confirm as fair simplification of the Constitutions of Clarendon dispute.
'Chroniclers say the king himself later came to the tomb in penance': confirm.
'He was proud, stubborn, sometimes hard to like' is an interpretive line about character; Keeper may soften or cut.
